cards.text: This psalm is from David, the shepherd who became Israel's king (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3). It's for anybody who's ever watched someone do wrong and get AHEAD for it, like the coworker who skips every step and STILL gets the corner office. David starts right there: don't fret over people who do evil.

cards.question: David says don't fret over people who do evil. What's the other thing he tells you not to do about people who do wrong?
Why not fret over evildoers? David says they ___ quickly like grass.

cards.text: So what do you do INSTEAD of fretting? David's list: trust in the LORD, do good, dwell in the land, cultivate faithfulness, and NOWHERE on it does it say stare at their vacation photos and get mad.

cards.question: Then David says to delight yourself in the LORD. What does he say the LORD will give you?
True or false: David says if you commit your way to the LORD and trust in Him, He will do it.

cards.text: Then David paints a picture: the LORD will bring forth your righteousness like the dawn, your justice like the noonday sun.
Then comes the hard one: be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him. I had YEARS in a junk drawer to practice waiting, and I STILL stand at the oven window like the cookies owe me money.

cards.question: David says to refrain from anger and abandon wrath. And don't fret, he says. It can only bring ___.

cards.text: And here's why you can let it go: the evildoers will be cut off, but those who hope in the LORD will inherit the land. So put the rolling pin DOWN, friend.
Then David says how long the wicked have left: yet a little while. A LITTLE while, friend, not one of those 'between 8 and 6' delivery windows.

cards.question: True or false: David says that after a little while, if you go looking for the wicked, you'll still find them hanging around.
The wicked won't be found. But who does David say will inherit the land and delight in abundant prosperity?

cards.text: Now David shows what the wicked are up to: they scheme against the righteous and gnash their teeth at them. Gnashing teeth, friend, that's the face of a man who just opened his electric bill.

cards.question: The wicked gnash their teeth at the righteous, but the Lord ___, seeing that their day is coming.

cards.text: And it gets serious. The wicked draw the sword and bend the bow to bring down the poor and needy and to slay those whose ways are upright.

cards.question: The wicked have their swords drawn against the upright. What does David say happens to those swords?

answers.text: They are taken by the king

cards.text: Next David puts two piles side by side: the little that the righteous have, and the abundance of many who are wicked. I spent years in a junk drawer owning exactly NOTHING, so honestly, friend, BOTH piles look amazing to me.

cards.question: True or false: David says the little that the righteous have is better than the abundance of many who are wicked.

cards.text: Why? Because the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD upholds the righteous.

cards.question: David says the LORD knows the days of the blameless. How long does he say their inheritance will last?

cards.text: And when hard times hit? In the time of evil the blameless won't be ashamed, and in the days of famine they'll be satisfied.

cards.question: David says the wicked and enemies of the LORD will vanish and fade away like ___.

cards.text: The wicked borrow and don't repay, but the righteous are gracious and giving. We ALL know that guy who says he'll pay you back Friday and never says WHICH Friday.
Those the LORD blesses will inherit the land, but the cursed will be destroyed.

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD takes no interest in the journey of the man whose steps He orders.
David says the LORD orders a man's steps. Even when that man falls, David says he won't be overwhelmed. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD is holding his hand
He always lands on his feet

cards.text: Then David gets personal. He says, "I once was young and now am old, yet never have I seen the righteous abandoned or their children begging for bread."

cards.question: David says the righteous are ever generous and quick to lend. What does he say about their children?

cards.text: David's advice now is simple: turn away from evil and do good, so you will abide forever.

cards.question: David gives a reason to turn from evil and do good. What does he say the LORD loves?

cards.text: The LORD won't forsake His saints, and the righteous will inherit the land and dwell in it forever. There's "inherit the land" again, friend, so hold on to that one.

cards.question: Now David describes the righteous man. He says the mouth of the righteous man utters ___.
True or false: David says the law of his God is in the righteous man's heart.

cards.text: And the righteous man's steps don't falter. But the wicked lie in wait for the righteous and seek to slay them.

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD will leave the righteous in the power of the wicked who are lying in wait for them.

cards.text: Then David says: wait for the LORD and keep His way, and He'll raise you up to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you'll see it.
Then David says he has seen a wicked, ruthless man flourishing like a well-rooted native tree. Big. Rooted. LOOKS like he's not going anywhere.

cards.question: David saw a wicked man flourishing like a well-rooted tree. What happened to that man?

answers.text: He passed away and was no more
He turned from his wicked ways
He grew richer than ever before

cards.text: Now David says to consider the blameless and observe the upright. Watch THEM, friend, not the guy with the flashy car and the shady paperwork.

cards.question: True or false: David says to consider the blameless and observe the upright, because hardship awaits the man of peace.

cards.text: But the transgressors will all be destroyed, and the future of the wicked will be cut off.
And the righteous? David says their salvation is from the LORD.

cards.question: David says the salvation of the righteous is from the LORD. What does he say the LORD is for them in time of trouble?
In the last line, David says the LORD helps the righteous and rescues them from the wicked. Why does He save them?

answers.text: Because they take refuge in Him
